extracted.intended_audience: USPTO stakeholders, trademark practitioners, registrants, TTAB participants, and USPTO staff/policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, requirements, and performance criteria governing USPTO trademark operations, IT modernization, TTAB procedures, fee policy, and efforts to preserve register integrity as described in the TPAC FY2019 report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of U.S. licensed attorney for foreign applicants/registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, registrants, and parties to proceedings whose domicile or principal place of business is not located in the United States must be represented by an attorney who is an active member in good standing of the bar of the highest court of a U.S. state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented August 3, 2019. Mirrors local counsel requirements in other countries; addresses unauthorized representation and reduces risk of invalid registrations due to improper signatures or use claims. Applied to Trademark Operations submissions and to TTAB proceedings (TTAB will suspend cases and set deadlines to obtain U.S. counsel when applicable). Expected effects include increased confidence in registrations and potential increases in filings against foreign-owned marks (and possible defaults).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory electronic filing (MEF) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend Rules of Practice to mandate electronic filing of trademark applications and submissions associated with trademark applications and registrations, and require designation of an email address for USPTO correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule published July 31, 2019 with planned implementation Dec 21, 2019; certain treaty-based exceptions apply. Purpose: enable end-to-end electronic processing, improve administrative efficiency, facilitate file management, optimize workflows, reduce processing errors, and stop subsidization of paper filers by electronic filers. Systems development and updates are required to support MEF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random audits of post-registration proof of use declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct random audits of 'proof of use' (post-registration maintenance affidavits) under 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.161(h) and 7.37(h) to improve the integrity of the Trademark Register by cancelling registrations with unsubstantiated use claims and removing unsupported goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019: over 5,000 files audited; in 62% of audited registrations, either a response deleting goods/services was filed or registration cancelled. In audited files, 78% of registrants were represented by an attorney and 22% were pro se. Goal: reduce unsubstantiated use claims and improve register accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Countermeasures to fraudulent solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase awareness and enforcement against companies fraudulently promising trademark protection or offering misleading solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include DOJ prosecution (two USPTO lawyers detailed to DOJ for two years), co-leading TM5 project on fraudulent solicitations, publishing web pages and a "Solicitation Alert" video, and stakeholder outreach. Emphasis on user education to recognize solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Specimen Analysis (specimen database) project
rubrics_metrics.description: Procure and integrate a commercial off-the-shelf tool permitting automated, integrated analysis of trademark specimens to detect fraudulent specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool will use metadata, error analysis, compression, filtering, and other methodologies to compare a specimen against others. To be used by Trademark employees as needed and integrated into workflow; beta testing expected late 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP record security enhancements
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance security around changes to critical parts of trademark records (e.g., email/correspondence addresses) to prevent malicious or unauthorized changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploring required user names, passwords, and PINs; in interim, USPTO sends emails to trademark owners/applicants when a change of correspondence address is received. Rationale: observed spike in malicious/damaging inputs and unauthorized address changes causing record-correction requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCIO priority: stabilization of legacy systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Stabilization to reduce risk of future system outages in infrastructure and existing systems; maintain and enhance current trademark systems until modernization is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted stabilization of two dozen systems based on risk and business criticality; FY2019 accomplishments included stabilization of TEAS, TEASi, TMNG CMS, and initiating stabilization of TRADEUPS, TTABIS, and TSDR. Funding increases were made to support stabilization. Stabilization addresses unsupported hardware, emergency maintenance costs, and availability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCIO priority: modernization and reuse of TMNG components
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernization efforts to improve agility, performance, stability, and deliver new features by reusing TMNG components where appropriate and integrating modern capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernization includes AI research to combat unauthorized changes, analytics tools, TEAS Plus Short Form widget, mobile apps, Trademark Quality Review improvements, CKEditor integration, and technical architecture reviews; aims for data management, automation, and AI to drive savings and speed to market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate legacy IT system risks and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess legacy trademark IT systems for planned retirement status, unsupported hardware/software, specialized skill dependencies, technology mixing, inflexibility, and security vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified challenges: systems beyond planned retirement, increasing emergency maintenance costs, reliance on specialized skills (risk if lost), mixed old/new technology complicating maintenance, inflexibility preventing adoption of new tech, and security issues with no available fixes. These are decision factors for stabilization vs replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Agile principles for IT modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow Agile methodology principles in trademark IT development: continuous awareness of project progress, stakeholder engagement, end-to-end implementation with small measurable successes, and incremental phased delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPAC commends focus on constant progress monitoring, communication, engagement of stakeholders, small measurable steps, and an incremental approach addressing critical gaps in real time before adding new products. Agile pilot teams began in FY2019. Emphasizes end-user acceptance and continuous feedback loops, including more Examining Attorney involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project governance and investment oversight criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure adequate oversight, capital planning, investment control, and project management for major IT investments (e.g., TMNG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found investment board members did not exercise adequate oversight to correct or terminate underperforming investments; weaknesses in CPIC process and ineffective project management for TMNG. USPTO is implementing OIG and consultant recommendations and refocusing delivery approaches. Governance adequacy is a criterion for project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-user acceptance and stakeholder involvement metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and prioritize end-user acceptance of IT products and involve Examining Attorneys and stakeholders in development to provide sound end-user guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG and consultant reviews identified end-user acceptance as critical. TPAC suggests improving Examining Attorney involvement to create continuous stakeholder feedback during development (consistent with Agile concepts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilization and modernization progress tracking (TMNG expenditures and outputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track cumulative investment, project milestones, technical reviews, product releases, and budget overruns for TMNG and related modernization efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TMNG cost from inception through FY2019 was $204.8M; project experienced delays and budget overruns. USPTO conducted program governance and architecture reviews and implemented recommendations. TPAC monitors spending and progress closely with OCIO and OCFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Reserve policy and targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an Operating Reserve with a minimum level ($75M) and an optimal target of six months of trademark operating expenses, with up to 25% acceptable planning variance and biennial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: mitigate variability in trademark fee collections and ensure cash flow to sustain operations. TPAC monitors reserve health and the impact of IT spending and appropriation lapses on reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting criteria and proposed fee adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Set and adjust trademark fees considering workload, filing forecasts, spending requirements, cost-to-revenue balance, and behavioral incentives that improve the quality of the Register and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO reviewed a 5-year financial outlook and proposed fee adjustments and new fees to address fiscal sustainability; TPAC held public hearings (e.g., Sept 23, 2019) and plans to implement changes based on public feedback (target Aug 2020). Fee adjustments should balance revenue needs against stakeholder impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Advisory Board (FAB) oversight role
rubrics_metrics.description: FAB provides oversight, accountability, and analysis for financial activities, including review of fee proposals and annual spending requests to ensure sufficient funding for USPTO mission and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAB co-chaired by the CFO and Commissioners; it revalidated FY2020 plans and the FY2021 OMB budget request. FAB evaluates consistency of practices to mitigate financial/operational risk and monitors delivery on performance commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and monitoring of direct vs indirect spending allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and evaluate allocation of trademark fee revenues between direct operations/TTAB and indirect administrative services, and compare allocation shares with patents to identify concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019: Trademark direct expenses (operations + TTAB) were 50.9% of trademark expenses; trademark & TTAB IT systems were 14.5%; including supported IT products, OCIO expenses were 17% of trademark expenses; administrative service allocations were ~29.6%. TPAC has raised concerns about allocation differences versus patents and will monitor and discuss adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor trademark IT spending as percentage of revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: Track trademark IT spending relative to trademark revenues and overall investments in modernization projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019 IT support accounted for 13.8% of trademark revenues; $204.8M invested in TMNG through Aug 2019. IT subcommittee and budget subcommittee coordinated to monitor budget versus spending for Trademark IT support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve trademark-focused capabilities in shared services arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: When participating in Department of Commerce Enterprise Services, ensure USPTO maintains access to mission-specific HR, payroll, financial management, and IT capabilities and that trademark user fees are not diverted to general DOC functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO agreed to maintain existing arrangements for payroll and HR under DOC shared services; TPAC is pleased that user fees are not being diverted. Mutually beneficial arrangements should protect trademark-specific needs and investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB workload management and staffing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Address surges in TTAB workload and staffing shortages by hiring additional Administrative Trademark Judges (ATJs) and Interlocutory Attorneys (IAs) and identifying opportunities for operational efficiencies to improve pendency and inventory control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019 saw increases in appeals and trials; trials comprised 33% of RFD inventory (up from ~23% in FY2016). TTAB is increasing personnel and seeking operational changes to reduce pendency; TPAC commends these actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited cancellation pilot program eligibility and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Select cancellation cases limited to abandonment and/or nonuse claims (not resulting in default) for participation in an expedited cancellation pilot where TTAB facilitates discovery conferences and encourages use of ACR techniques to resolve cases more quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot began March 2018; as of end of FY2019, 160 cases eligible and ~80 conferences held; only 15 proceedings agreed at discovery conference to use some form of ACR. Parties' reluctance often stems from need for discovery to prove abandonment/nonuse; TTAB will continue pilot and gather feedback via follow-up interviews to assess what did/didn't work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage use of Alternative Case Resolution (ACR) techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: At discovery conferences, TTAB encourages parties to use pre-existing ACR techniques to expedite proceedings and resolve disputes without full trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACR may speed removal of unused marks from the register but parties often decline to forgo discovery. TTAB seeks to learn which procedures parties are willing to agree to and why parties are not willing to commit to expedited procedures early in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor default judgment rates as a performance metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Track default judgment rates in cancellation proceedings (overall and by claim type) to inform policy on expedited procedures and resource allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB data (Feb 26, 2018–Jul 20, 2019): overall default rate for cancellations 45%; cancellations including abandonment/nonuse 51%; cancellations without those claims 29%; only-abandonment 62%; only-nonuse 53%. High default rates inform skepticism about stakeholder interest in formal expedited cancellation rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual TBMP revision practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board Manual of Procedure (TBMP) annually to incorporate recent case law and reflect current TTAB practice and procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: June 2019 TBMP revision incorporated case law from March 2, 2018 to March 1, 2019. Regular updates follow the annual revision schedule to keep guidance current for practitioners and the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Protective Order (SPO) confidentiality and access policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Default protective order applies in inter partes TTAB proceedings (unless parties agree otherwise), with current presumptions regarding in-house counsel access to 'Attorneys' Eyes Only' (AEO) materials and a two-tier confidentiality structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB solicited stakeholder comments in 2018-2019 on (1) in-house counsel presumptive access to AEO material and (2) whether to reintroduce a 'highly confidential' tier. Comments were split; TTAB unlikely to alter the non-access presumption or reintroduce a third tier absent strong reason, but will address outstanding issues and introduce a revised SPO. TTAB also considers entering the SPO into prosecution history to make it of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit and incorporate stakeholder feedback systematically
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seek and use stakeholder input (public comments, hearings, follow-up interviews) to inform rulemaking, pilot programs, and procedural changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: extended comment deadlines for SPO feedback, public hearing on proposed fee adjustments, and suggested follow-up interviews with counsel who completed the expedited cancellation pilot to obtain detailed feedback on what worked and what didn't.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure TTAB performance via pendency and inventory metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use performance measures such as average pendency, inventory control, appeals becoming RFD, and trial case proportions to assess TTAB health and identify operational needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019 saw increased trials and appeals; longer pendency and inventory weighted toward trial cases. TPAC monitors these metrics and commends steps to improve productivity (hiring, procedural changes).
